what: Divide the square of the panel’s long side into N×N cells (default 12), place a bold quarter arc in each cell and draw the lines out (a curve that comes out over 2s). The ”rings” type turns cells so that 2×2 cells form one ring and empties one piece per ring, while the rings in the first and last few rows have just one piece in a lighter color. Each ring starts 0~2s late. The ”random” type has a random direction per cell. With erase on, after drawing it pauses .2s, then erases toward the same side (a curve going in) and disappears. Used for the opening curtain.

options.n: Cells per side, default 12 (opening act 5, phone 4)
options.width: Line thickness (one cell side : 100), default 20 — 64 for the opening curtain
options.dur: Length of one cell (s), default 2 — with erase, the total of draw, hold and erase
options.stagger: Random delay per cell (ring) in seconds, default 2 — 0 means all at once
options.gap: Gap between cells (share of one cell side), default .1
options.look: rings (default — 2×2 cell rings) · random (random direction per cell)
options.hide: on leaves one piece empty in each of the rings, default on
options.accent: Only one piece lighter in the rings of the outermost few rows at both ends, default 0 (original About section 2, phone 4)
options.erase: if on, draws then pauses and erases (opening cover), once fully erased the element gets an arc-grid-draw:done event
options.hold: Hold time (sec) when it stops fully drawn with erase, default .2
options.on: scroll (default — when visible) · load (as soon as it attaches)
options.--fx-arc / --fx-arc-accent: Line color and pale fragment color (via style) — default --kf-ink · --kf-dim

from.where: index.html .ix-about__rings (About section pattern — original Framer code component count 12 · strokeWidth 20 · durationSeconds 2 · stagger 2 · gap .1 · randomHideQuarter · accentColumns 2) · .ix-pre (opening curtain — count 5 · strokeWidth 64 · randomRotation · erasePhase · phaseGap .2, phone 4)

note: Each time it opens, the cleared pieces and delays are random, so it is not the same picture as the original. With reduced motion, it shows the end state of the drawing (for erase it disappears at once and is done)
